title: The Grateful River Fisherman (ZH)
summary: A fisherman finds a lost royal emerald in the stomach of a fish and returns it to Akbar. Birbal ensures the honest man's reward blesses his village.
full_text:
While boating upon the river Yamuna during a festival, Emperor Akbar slipped his favorite emerald signet ring from his finger, and it splashed into the deep, swirling waters, sinking forever out of sight. Divers searched for two days, but found nothing.

A week later, an impoverished river fisherman named Mangal caught a colossal carp three leagues downriver. While cleaning the fish for his family's dinner, his knife struck something hard inside the fish's belly. Wiping away the scales, he uncovered the gleaming imperial signet ring, engraved with Akbar's royal seal!

The fisherman's wife gasped: 'Husband! This emerald can buy us five houses and make us rich for life! Let us sell it to a jeweler in Delhi!'

Mangal shook his head firmly: 'No, wife. This ring bears the imperial seal of our Emperor. What is found must be returned to its owner. Dishonest bread brings a curse upon the children.'

The next morning, Mangal walked to the Agra palace in his patched rags, knelt before the throne, and presented the emerald ring to Akbar.

Akbar was overjoyed: 'Fisherman, you have restored my father's heirloom! Ask for whatever reward you desire!'

Mangal bowed humbly: 'Sire, I am an uneducated fisherman. If you give me gold coins, I may lose them to thieves.

'I ask only this: build a small stone school and a clean drinking water well in our riverside village, so that our children may learn to read and write and our wives need not walk miles for water.'

The entire court was hushed by the peasant's selfless request.

Birbal stepped forward, his eyes shining with admiration:

'Sire, look at the nobility of this honest fisherman. A greedy nobleman would have asked for titles, land, and gold for himself.

'This poor man asks only for knowledge and clean water for his neighbors! True virtue thinks not of its own pocket, but of the community's future.'

Akbar ordered the school and well built immediately, appointed Mangal the royal superintendent of the river fisheries with a handsome salary, and rewarded Birbal for celebrating the pure hearts of the people.
